CMF – Turning Ideas into Impact.

Wir machen aus „How?" ein „Wow!" mit kreativer Strategie, innovativer Technologie und messbarem Impact. Wir sind eine Full-Service-Agentur und vereinen alle Disziplinen unter einem Dach, ob digital oder analog, klassisch oder crazy, und entwickeln seit über 42 Jahren für namhafte Kunden wie Allianz, Coca-Cola, BMW, Nestlé und Rewe Kampagnen, die begeistern. Verstärke unser rund 100-köpfiges Team am Standort Oberursel als:

Performance Marketing Manager (m/w/d)

Aufgaben
Du sorgst mit klarer Zielgruppenplanung, durchdachten Kampagnen-Setups und sauberem Tracking dafür, dass Kampagnen von Tag eins an funktionieren. Cost-per-Lead, Click-through-Rate, Conversion-Rate sind für dich die Stellschrauben, die du von Beginn an präzise justierst. Bei CMF machst du das für Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn und TikTok und für namhafte Kunden mit echten Ansprüchen, bei denen man spürbar etwas bewegen kann.

Und wenn sich ein Algorithmus ändert, bist du die erste Person im Raum, die weiß, was das für unsere Kampagnen bedeutet.

Qualifikation

Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Performance Marketing, mit echtem Budget und echter Verantwortung.

Sicherer Umgang mit Google Ads (Search, Display, Video) und Meta Ads, von der Einrichtung bis zur Auswertung.

Erfahrung mit A/B-Tests und Conversion-Optimierung: Du verbesserst, was schon gut läuft.

SEO-Wissen, technisch wie redaktionell, und ein Blick für GEO. Du weißt, wie Inhalte heute auch in ChatGPT oder Google AI Overviews gefunden werden.

Routine mit Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager und Looker Studio. Attribution und Tracking sind für dich Alltag.

Interesse an KI-Tools und Automatisierung, um Kampagnen effizienter zu steuern und mehr Zeit für die Strategie zu gewinnen.

Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch, denn unsere Meetings mit Kunden und im Team laufen auf Deutsch. Gutes Englisch hilft dir bei internationalen Kunden.

Du kennst Trends und Kanäle und erarbeitest gemeinsam mit Text, Kreation überzeugende Journeys und Creatives.

Du berätst Kunden auf Augenhöhe und erklärst Zahlen und Empfehlungen verständlich und triffst gemeinsam mit ihnen fundierte Entscheidungen für ihre Kampagnen.

Benefits
Ein Team mit kurzen Wegen und echter Entscheidungsfreude. Hybrides Arbeiten, flexible Zeiten, Projekte, die sich nie wiederholen. Ein modernes, klimafreundliches Büro in Oberursel mit eigener Bar. Dazu Team-Events, auf die man sich wirklich freut.

Ready to make impact?

We are seeking an **experienced, expert\-level Marketing \& Brand Strategist** to work directly with the Founder/CEO in developing and executing marketing, brand, content, and growth strategies across a portfolio of businesses in healthcare, mental health, insurance, financial services, education, entrepreneurship, and personal development.

We are looking for someone who understands how to take a business objective and translate it into a compelling **marketing strategy, brand position, campaign, content plan, and lead\-generation strategy that produces measurable growth.**

The ideal candidate combines high\-level strategic thinking with strong creative execution. You should be able to develop the strategy, shape the messaging, create or direct the visuals, leverage AI, launch campaigns, and analyze what is actually producing results.

**Marketing \& Growth Strategy**

* Develop and execute marketing and brand strategies across multiple businesses
* Translate business goals into campaigns that generate awareness, qualified leads, appointments, enrollments, and customers

jobs.description:
Creative Marketing Translators \& Transcreators \| Spanish (Puerto Rico)
Acclaro is currently recruiting up to **2 Creative Marketing Translators \& Transcreators** **(English \> Spanish (Puerto Rico))** to support ongoing marketing, entertainment, and multimedia localization projects for an active global client.


This remote freelance opportunity is open to experienced linguists who have an exceptional command of **Spanish as used in Puerto Rico** and the creativity to adapt marketing, entertainment, and multimedia content for Puerto Rican audiences.


You will help global brands deliver engaging, culturally relevant content while preserving their voice, creative intent, and marketing impact.


Position Overview* **Language Pair:** English to Spanish for Puerto Rico
* **Domain:** Marketing, Entertainment, and Creative Content
* **Experience:** 3\+ years of translation and creative transcreation experience
* **Contract Type:** Freelance / Independent Contractor
* **Engagement Type:** Project\-Based with Ongoing Opportunities
* **Location:** Remote
* **Compensation:** This is a paid freelance opportunity. Compensation will be determined based on the candidate's proposed rates and project requirements.


Responsibilities* Translate and creatively adapt **marketing, entertainment and multimedia content** to engage and resonate with local audiences.
* Work collaboratively with internal and linguistic teams to ensure high quality output across various platforms.
* Conduct research to understand cultural nuances, ensuring that translations are not just literal but culturally relevant.
* Review and provide feedback on marketing projects to contribute to their success.

  

**Requirements**  

* Native\-level proficiency in **Spanish for Puerto Rico** and a strong understanding of Puerto Rican culture, consumer behavior, and marketing communication styles.
* Proven experience of **3 or more years in translation and transcreation**, preferably in a marketing context.
* Bachelor's degree in **Translation, Marketing, Linguistics, or a related field**.
* Strong understanding of marketing principles and the ability to adapt tone and style to fit various brand guidelines; experience with entertainment or global brand content is a plus.
* Experience translating or transcreating multimedia entertainment content, including TV series and movie synopses, title localization, PR, and other creative content related to TV and movie entertainment, is a plus.
* Experience with CAT tools is a plus.


Application Process
The selection process consists of the following stages:

* **Application review**
* **One\-way video interview**, taking approximately **15 to 20 minutes**, which candidates can complete at a convenient time within the specified deadline
* **Translation and transcreation assessment** to evaluate the linguistic, creative, and cultural skills required for the project
* **Secure identity verification** for candidates selected for the project
* **Onboarding to Acclaro’s systems,** followed by **project\-specific training and onboarding**




Successful completion of each stage is required to be considered for a freelance engagement. All personal information is handled securely for recruitment, contracting, and compliance purposes.

 **Benefits**  

* **Flexible Remote Work:** Work from anywhere, managing your own hours around project deadlines.
* **Long\-Term Collaboration Opportunities:** We aim to build lasting partnerships with our freelance linguists; successful candidates will become part of our preferred talent pool for ongoing, periodic project assignments.
* **Cutting\-Edge Tech:** Gain experience working with advanced localization workflows, AI\-driven translation tools, and global brand content.
* **Elite Projects:** Build your portfolio by working on software utilized by millions of global users daily.


About Acclaro
Acclaro combines cultural and language expertise with AI technology to help brands grow their global presence, connect with customers, and mean something to them. As a trusted partner to some of the world’s biggest brands and fastest\-growing global companies, our mission is to harness the powerful combination of human expertise and cutting\-edge technology. We focus on putting brands into the heads, hearts, and hands of people everywhere.


Our AI\-powered business management and language platform ensures a faster time to market with measurable results, while our global team of language, country, and technology experts crafts localization strategies that empower our customers to succeed in any market.

jobs.title: Account Director - Agency
jobs.description:
**Account Director – Client \& Affiliate Management**

**Position Summary**

The Account Director is responsible for the strategic leadership, growth, and overall performance of assigned client accounts, while also overseeing the affiliate and media partner relationships that support client delivery.

This role serves as a senior point of contact for clients and is accountable for translating client objectives into actionable performance strategies, coordinating internal teams and external partners, monitoring campaign and lead performance, and ensuring commitments related to volume, quality, cost, and service are achieved.

The Account Director operates as both a client advocate and business owner, balancing client expectations with campaign performance, partner capabilities, profitability, and the company’s broader strategic objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Client Relationship \& Account Leadership**

* Serve as the senior day\-to\-day relationship owner for assigned client accounts.
* Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders and develop a strong understanding of their business objectives, enrollment goals, target audiences, performance expectations, and operational requirements.
* Lead regular client meetings, business reviews, campaign performance discussions, and strategic planning sessions.
* Translate client objectives into clear priorities and execution plans for internal teams and external partners.
* Proactively identify performance concerns, emerging risks, and opportunities and provide clients with clear recommendations and solutions.
* Manage client expectations regarding lead volume, quality, cost, pacing, targeting, and campaign performance.
* Ensure client questions, issues, and escalations are addressed promptly and appropriately.
* Maintain a strong understanding of contractual commitments, campaign requirements, pricing, budgets, and service expectations.

**Affiliate \& Partner Management**

* Manage relationships with affiliate, publisher, lead\-generation, and other external media partners supporting assigned accounts.
* Communicate campaign requirements, targeting criteria, lead specifications, compliance expectations, pricing, volume goals, and quality standards to partners.
* Evaluate affiliate performance using metrics including lead volume, acceptance rates, rejection rates, cost per lead, cost per acquisition, lead quality, conversion performance, and return on investment.
* Monitor lead delivery and identify trends related to filtered, rejected, returned, duplicate, or otherwise non\-compliant leads.
* Hold partners accountable for agreed\-upon performance, quality, compliance, and delivery standards.
* Work with affiliates to optimize campaigns, improve lead quality, adjust volume, resolve performance concerns, and identify opportunities to scale.
* Recommend increasing, reducing, pausing, or terminating partner allocations based on performance.
* Develop strong relationships with high\-performing partners and identify opportunities to expand productive affiliate relationships.
* Assist with sourcing, evaluating, and onboarding new affiliate and media partners where appropriate.

**Revenue \& Account Growth**

* Own the health, retention, and growth of assigned accounts.
* Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships through increased volume, additional programs, new campaigns, services, products, or media channels.
* Partner with leadership and Business Development on account expansion opportunities.
* Understand account economics, including revenue, partner costs, pricing, gross margin, and profitability.
* Monitor account and partner performance to ensure delivery models remain financially sustainable.
* Participate in forecasting client revenue, campaign volume, and partner allocations.
* Support renewals, pricing discussions, scope changes, and contract extensions as appropriate.

**Cross\-Functional Leadership**

* Serve as the central point of coordination across Client Success, Media, Operations, Analytics, Creative, Product, and other teams supporting assigned accounts.
* Establish clear priorities, responsibilities, timelines, and expectations for account\-related initiatives.
* Ensure internal teams have the information necessary to execute client requirements effectively.
* Facilitate resolution of issues that cross functional or organizational boundaries.
* Escalate material client, partner, financial, compliance, or performance risks to leadership when appropriate.
* Provide clear and timely communication regarding account performance, changes in client priorities, and emerging risks.

**Compliance \& Lead Quality**

* Ensure affiliates and media partners comply with client requirements, company standards, applicable advertising requirements, and campaign\-specific restrictions.
* Partner with internal Compliance, Operations, and Technology teams to investigate lead\-quality or compliance concerns.
* Monitor patterns in rejected, filtered, returned, or disputed leads and work with appropriate teams to determine root causes.
* Ensure partner remediation plans are established when quality or compliance issues are identified.
* Maintain appropriate documentation of significant client and partner performance issues and agreed\-upon corrective actions.

**Performance Measures**

Success in the role may be measured by:

* Client retention and satisfaction
* Account revenue growth
* Gross margin and account profitability
* Achievement of client volume and pacing objectives
* Lead acceptance and delivery rates
* Lead quality and downstream conversion performance
* Cost per lead / cost per acquisition
* Affiliate performance and partner optimization
* Resolution of client and partner issues
* Forecast accuracy
* Identification and execution of account expansion opportunities
* Compliance with client and company requirements

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related

jobs.title: Content Director, Rex Media
jobs.description:
**Company Overview**
Rex is a privately held ecosystem of entrepreneurial ventures led by Peter Rex, spanning real estate private equity, technology, insurance, and AI. We build businesses and investment platforms that generate both exceptional financial returns and meaningful societal impact. At the core of our strategy is investor engagement: attracting aligned capital partners who share our long\-term vision. We are building the most compelling investor\-facing ecosystem in the private markets. The role offers exposure to a uniquely diverse platform, combining institutional\-quality real estate and high\-growth tech ventures, all aligned under a singular mission\-driven vision.  

  

**About Us**
Our mission is to catalyze human flourishing through stewardship, serving people in all nations. We seek a transcendent impact, second to none, crossing geographies and making a permanent mark on history.
We aim to uplift investors, foster flourishing families, create enduring trust, and contribute to a more beautiful world through our investments, products and services, and new ventures.
Our investments are primarily in real estate, with additional allocations to tech, energy, and alternatives, employing a downside\-protected, long\-term approach to investing. We are grounded in timeless morals and seek to preserve and grow both investor capital and our own.
We serve a diverse ecosystem that includes:  

  

* Multifamily apartment management with 20,000\+ apartments
* Hotel and office buildings
* Tech ventures
* Insurance companies
  

  

Our businesses, with over 500 employees, are primarily throughout Texas and Florida, but we aim to expand globally with our products and services, impacting people in all countries.  

  

**Mindset**
* Fanatical Investor Focus: Serve our investors by preserving their wealth first and foremost and secondarily seeking to maximize their return on equity while fostering human progress through stewardship of the assets and companies.
* Ecosystem Alignment: Execute in a spirit of partnership across all components of the Rex ecosystem, including multifamily and other real estate assets as well as tech companies.
* Missionary Zeal: Care about investor stewardship and advancing the vision of catalyzing human flourishing.
  

  

**The Opportunity**
Rex is seeking a Content Director, Rex Media to take ownership of our entire media presence and turn it into a growth engine for the business, not just a content calendar. This is a video\-first mandate: the flagship output is high\-quality video, with written and short\-form content flowing out from it, not produced separately. This role is anchored by three core mandates. Own the planning and production of video content that drives measurable growth in following, engagement, and new business, with a proven history of doing exactly that. Master the full funnel, building top, middle, and end of funnel content assets and owning the mechanism that turns engagement into actual customers and investors, not just impressions. Keep every platform cranking, including LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube and YouTube Shorts, using external execution partners where it creates leverage, such as engagement, commenting, and production support, while retaining full ownership of strategy and quality. The ideal candidate has 7 to 12 years of deep, hands\-on experience in content creation and social media, with a demonstrated command of the platform game and a track record that speaks for itself. They have real proficiency in business, finance, and investment concepts, enough to know where to cut a video, which themes will land, and how to speak credibly to a sophisticated audience. They know how to create content that lures attention while still delivering genuine value to a UHNW investor audience, balancing virality with substance. Like all Rex players, they are proactive and resourceful, take the initiative without waiting to be told, and treat obstacles as something to solve rather than escalate. Must be missionary minded, driven to further human flourishing primarily through the stewardship of investor capital and secondarily through how that capital is put to work across real estate, tech, and beyond. Not for mercenaries. Only for missionaries. Fully remote.  

  

#### **About the Role**


Rex is hiring a Content Director, Rex Media to run the company's entire media presence as a business function with a P\&L mindset, not a creative side project. This role owns outcomes, not just output: growth in following and engagement matters, but only insofar as it converts into real investor and customer pipeline.  

  

Video is the center of gravity. jobs.description:
Hometown Soccer Holdings (HSH) is building locally rooted MLS NEXT Pro clubs, deeply connected to their communities and poised for long\-term success. Across a growing portfolio, every campaign, matchday, product drop, and announcement generates daily creative demand that outside agencies are poorly suited to serve efficiently. The Creative Services Manager will bring high\-volume creative production in\-house, owning the assets, template systems, and creative workflow that keep every club on brand and moving quickly.  


Reporting to the Vice President of Marketing, this role will produce the social, paid, email, merchandise, matchday, and presentation creative that HSH and its clubs need day to day, and will build the campaign and club launch template systems local teams can populate themselves. The Creative Services Manager will own creative request intake, prioritization, and service levels across clubs and central functions, and will coordinate agencies and freelancers for overflow and specialized work.  


This is a builder's opportunity for a fast, versatile designer who thinks in systems rather than one\-off files. The ideal candidate brings a strong multi\-channel portfolio, demonstrated experience building template systems that other people actually used, and the discipline to work at volume without losing brand craft.  

**Responsibilities:** **Creative Production**  

* Own high\-volume day\-to\-day creative production across all clubs and central functions
* Produce social graphics, paid media assets, email and website graphics, matchday and promotional creative
* Support merchandise graphics and product storytelling assets
* Build presentation decks and sponsorship mockups in support of Sponsorship and Ticket Sales needs
* Support club launch materials across every market ahead of the 2027 season

 **Template \& Asset Systems**  

* Build campaign and club launch template systems local teams can populate themselves
* Maintain the asset library, naming conventions, and version control so assets are findable and current
* Execute and uphold brand guidelines across all daily creative output
* Keep club creative visually consistent with the portfolio brand without flattening local identity
* Reduce agency dependency for recurring production work and document what stays in\-house versus what goes out

 **Creative Workflow \& Request Management**  

* Own creative request intake, prioritization, and published service levels across clubs and central functions
* Maintain a production calendar visible to clubs and central stakeholders
* Coordinate agencies and freelancers for overflow and specialized work, including briefing and quality control
* Escalate capacity conflicts with options
* Feed performance learnings from Performance \& Lifecycle Marketing back into creative direction

 **Club Enablement \& Local Partnership**  

* Turn local asset requests around within published service levels
* Train local content contributors on template use, brand guardrails, and asset standards
* Capture market\-specific inputs and content from clubs and route them into the asset library
* Support local content capture standards in partnership with Fan Engagement and Communications
* Own the creative segment of the recurring central/local operating cadence
* Additional duties as assigned.

  

**Qualifications**  

* 5\+ years of experience in graphic design, creative production, or creative operations.
* Strong portfolio spanning social, digital and paid media, email, and print.
* Expert command of Adobe Creative Suite including Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, plus template systems in Figma or comparable tools.
* Demonstrated experience building template or design systems that other people used successfully.
* Experience managing a creative request queue with competing stakeholders and defending prioritization.
* Basic motion and video editing capability in After Effects, Premiere, or comparable tools.
* Ability to work at volume and speed without losing brand discipline.
* Experience in sports or live entertainment creative, or supporting multi\-brand or multi\-location organizations, is strongly preferred.

 **EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**  

Hometown Soccer Holdings is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a staff that reflects the communities our clubs play in. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available at any point in the application or employment process.

jobs.title: Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Description

Purpose

The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer is responsible for preparing and submitting air quality permit applications for Teichert Materials stationary and portable equipment operations across California and western Nevada. The primary focus of this role is permitting: compiling emissions data for reporting, quantifying source emissions, preparing Authority to Construct (ATC) and Permit to Operate (PTO) applications, and managing them through district review to issuance.

This role serves as the company's technical resource for New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT) and toxics evaluations, CARB portable equipment (PERP) registration, and coordination with local air districts, the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), and Northern Nevada Public Health. The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer supports facility- and equipment-level compliance, tracks permit conditions and renewal deadlines, and drives regulatory readiness and risk mitigation across the Teichert Family of Companies.

Focus & Scope

Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:

Air Quality Permitting and Regulatory Analysis

Prepare, submit, and manage complete and technically defensible air quality permit applications for new, modified, relocated, stationary, and portable equipment and sources, including Authority to Construct (ATC), Permit to Operate (PTO), and applicable portable equipment registrations.
Quantify source-specific emissions, including NOx, SOx, CO, VOC, PM/PM10/PM2.5, and toxic air contaminants, using applicable regulatory methodologies, emission factors, and accepted calculation methods.
Evaluate projects, facilities, and equipment to determine applicable permitting requirements, including exemptions, New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT), offsets, air toxics requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements.
Review draft permit conditions prior to ATC issuance, and negotiate practical, enforceable condition language with district permit engineers to minimize operational and compliance burden while meeting air quality standards.
Manage permit applications through agency review and issuance, including responding to completeness determinations, deficiency notices, and technical inquiries; evaluating proposed permit conditions; and working with regulatory agencies to establish practical and enforceable permit requirements.
Coordinate air quality permitting with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and other regulatory processes when applicable.

Regulatory Compliance and Reporting

Maintain and administer air quality permits, registrations, compliance obligations, and regulatory deadlines for Company operations, including permit and registration renewals, monitoring, recordkeeping, emissions inventories, testing, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and submit required air quality regulatory reports and inventories, including applicable criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant reporting, CARB Criteria and Toxics Reporting (CTR), greenhouse gas reporting, and AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” reporting.
Administer applicable AB 2588 requirements, including toxic air contaminant emissions inventories, prioritization and risk screening, and coordination of required health risk assessments, public notifications, or risk-reduction activities.
Coordinate and oversee source (stack) testing for stationary equipment — scheduling required tests with certified testing firms, preparing and submitting source test protocols for district approval, coordinating district witnessing, and reviewing test reports for compliance with permit conditions and applicable emission limits.
Monitor facility and equipment compliance with applicable permit conditions and regulatory requirements, including fuel usage, throughput, hours of operation, emission limits, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations; identify compliance risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

Technical Evaluation and Field Support

Regularly access and evaluate active materials facilities, plants, equipment areas, and project sites to conduct source evaluations, obtain equipment and operational information, observe operating conditions, and support permitting and compliance activities (approximately 30% of work time, with the remaining time performing office-based permitting, analysis, and reporting functions). Site conditions may include uneven terrain, stairs or elevated areas, heavy moving equipment, dust, noise, and outdoor weather conditions.
Conduct or coordinate on-site evaluations of Company facilities, equipment, and project sites to identify applicable air quality permitting and compliance requirements and obtain technical and operational information necessary to support regulatory determinations, applications, and reporting.
Coordinate required source testing and other compliance evaluations, including test planning, regulatory agency coordination, review of technical results, and identification and resolution of potential compliance issues.
Provide technical guidance to operations, equipment, environmental, and project teams regarding air quality permitting and compliance requirements so regulatory considerations can be addressed during project planning, equipment acquisition or relocation, installation, and ongoing operations.

Agency and Organizational Representation

Serve as a Company technical representative and liaison with local Air Pollution Control Districts and Air Quality Management Districts, the California Air Resources Board (CARB), Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Northern Nevada Public Health (NNPH), consultants, testing firms, vendors, and other external parties regarding air quality permitting and compliance matters.
Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, enforcement matters, and corrective actions by evaluating compliance issues, assembling technical documentation, responding to regulatory inquiries, and developing or coordinating appropriate corrective action plans.
Represent the Company, as appropriate, in industry groups and regulatory proceedings; monitor emerging air quality laws and regulations; evaluate potential impacts to Company operations; and assist in developing comments or recommendations regarding proposed regulatory changes.

Compliance Systems and Risk Management

Develop and maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready permitting and compliance records, calculation tools, application templates, tracking systems, procedures, and other documentation necessary to support regulatory compliance and continuity of operations.
Maintain expert and current knowledge of applicable federal, California, Nevada, and local air quality requirements and evaluate regulatory developments that may affect Company operations.
Provide management with timely information regarding pending permit applications, regulatory deadlines, deficiencies, emerging requirements, and compliance risks, including recommended actions, responsible parties, and appropriate timelines for resolution.
Develop and improve permitting, workflow, and compliance processes, tools, and documentation to promote consistency, regulatory readiness, operational efficiency, and sustainable compliance across Company operations.

Relationships, Qualifications & Requirements, And Competencies

Key Relationships

Reports To

Environmental Manager, Teichert Materials

Direct Reports

N/A

External Clients

Public agencies, federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, subcontractors, vendors, general public

Internal Clients

President of Teichert Materials; Director of Aggregate Resource Development (ARD) and Environmental Compliance; Teichert Materials Plant Managers, Superintendents, and Administrative Staff; Teichert Services Group; ARD; Data and Technology Services (DTS); and other business units

Education

Bachelor's degree in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental science, or a related technical field preferred; equivalent combination of training, education, and experience will be considered.

Experience and Industry Expertise

Minimum of five (5) to eight (8) years of experience preparing air quality permit applications (Authority to Construct / Permit to Operate) for stationary or portable sources in California; experience with a California air district or as a permitting consultant preferred.
Working knowledge of the California local air district permitting system, New Source Review, BACT, air toxics evaluation, and CARB programs including PERP.
Experience with western Nevada air permitting (NDEP Bureau of Air Pollution Control and/or Northern Nevada Public Health) a plus.
Experience in the construction, aggregates, ready-mix, asphalt, or heavy equipment industries a plus.

Specific Job Requirements

Demonstrated ability to quantify source emissions using accepted emission factors and calculation methods, and to prepare complete, defensible permit applications.
Working understanding of how CEQA review interacts with air district permitting timelines.
Working knowledge of California AB 2588 (Air Toxics “Hot Spots”) requirements, including toxic emissions inventory, prioritization, and health risk assessment triggers.
Ability to interpret and apply federal, state, and local air quality regulations and to translate permit conditions into practical compliance requirements for field staff.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy; self-motivated with strong follow-through on applications and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to negotiate permit conditions with district engineers and to explain requirements to non-technical staff in plain language.
Strong organizational and time-management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent applications and shifting district review timelines.
Strong project management skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel for emissions calculations, and the ability to quickly learn permitting and database tools.
Collaborative team player able to thrive in a matrixed management structure across multiple operating groups.
Commitment to workplace safety and support of corporate safety initiatives.
Willingness to adhere to the Company Code of Conduct consistently.
Some travel required to job sites and district offices in California and western Nevada.
Ability to travel regularly to Company facilities, project sites, regulatory agency offices, and other business locations throughout California and western Nevada.
A valid driver's license and acceptable driving record are required when operating a motor vehicle on Company business.
May require occasional work outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends, to support regulatory deadlines, site activities, meetings, training, or time-sensitive operational matters.

Desirable Qualifications

Understanding of the working relationship between the CARB Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) and the Diesel Off-Road Online Reporting System (DOORS), including how portable and off-road diesel equipment is registered, reported, and kept compliant at both stationary facilities and temporary project sites.
Familiarity with distinguishing when equipment at a job site should be permitted by the local district, registered under PERP, or reported through DOORS, and how those pathways interact as equipment moves between sites.
Professional certification or coursework in air quality, environmental engineering, or a related field (e.g., QEP, CPEA, or equivalent).

Competencies

Building Relationships
Listening
Planning/Prioritizing
Initiative
Dependability
Judgement/Decision Making
Learning/Development
Managerial Courage
Safety

Equipment Used, Physical Demands, and Work Environment

From conducting streamflow measurements during high\-flow events to deploying cutting edge monitoring technology in remote locations, you will play a key role in collecting the data that informs important environmental and water management decisions.

 **What’s on Offer**

* Attractive salary \& use of company vehicle for site visits
* Field work Monday to Thursday and catch up in the office with your team on Fridays
* Flexibility around start and finish times
* Career development, upskilling and training opportunities
* Small collaborative and supportive team
* Access to a variety of Health and Wellness initiatives \- including the EAP, Ventia's Healthy Minds program and Healthy Bodies program
* Employee benefits such as corporate travel discounts, Novated leases, private health discounts, credit discounts with retailers Australia wide including Woolworths, Coles, Booking.com and Expedia

 **About the Role**  

This hands\-on role combines fieldwork, advanced technology, data analysis, and problem solving, offering the opportunity to build expertise across a wide range of environmental disciplines. You will work with industry leading equipment including ADCPs, water quality skills in hydrography, environmental monitoring and data management.

  

Whether you are troubleshooting a monitoring station, surveying river cross\-sections, collecting groundwater samples, or analysing complex environmental datasets, you will be part of a team delivering meaningful outcomes for some of Australia’s most significant environmental projects.

  

Under the guidance of the Regional Manager, you will –

* Conduct field based environmental monitoring of surface and groundwater systems
* Collect, analyse, and report streamflow and water quality data
* Install and maintain hydrometric stations and instrumentation
* Perform site surveys, discharge measurements, and cross\-sectional profiling using ADV’s and ADCP’s
* Manage data using platform such HYDSTRA, ESDAT and Campbells
* Ensure compliance with OH\&S protocols and maintain high data quality standards
* Coordinate with laboratories and stakeholders throughout project lifecycles

 **Required Skills and Experience**

* Experienced in groundwater / surface water monitoring
* Enrolled in or completed a Diploma in Water Operations or Bachelor of Environmental Science (or similar)
* Proficient in Microsoft Excel and familiar with hydrological software
* Skilled in using SDI\-12 and 4\-20mA instrumentation
* A strong communicator with excellent time management and self\-motivation
* Willing to travel including overnight stays
* Certified in First Aid and CPR
* White / Red Card desirable
* Current drivers licence (4x4 driving certification and experience – desirable)

 **About Ventia**  

As a leading services provider, we maintain, operate, and manage the essential infrastructure that makes modern life possible across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 35,000 employees and subcontractors across 400 sites, joining Ventia means becoming part of a team that values its people, supports career growth, and helps everyone go further towards their full potential.  

  

Our commitment to Fairness, Inclusion and Respect shapes how we lead, collaborate, hire and support one another. We are dedicated to providing an accessible recruitment process and encourage you to request adjustments at any stage.

jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

The Drinking Water Market Sector (“MS”) Business Development Director (BDD) will lead the development and implementation of business strategies across all HDR geographies in coordination with Market Sector and Regional Business Group leadership, operational leadership, client managers and Business Class Directors.   Reporting to the Director of Market Sector Development, and in full coordination with the Water Business Group leadership, the Drinking Water BDD creates and monitors frequent and regular communication across the Sector to drive top-line NFB growth and to implement the Drinking Water sector’s strategic initiatives, growth plans and marketing opportunities for the market sector. This market leader will support and collaborate across all HDR market sectors, regions, areas and business lines to advance a variety of strategies intended to grow services across the market sector. 

Drinking Water Market Sector–
Within the Water Business Group, the Drinking Water MS is a highly technical and diversified sector.  This reflects that this service offering routinely works for local municipalities, private entities, distinct water utilities, Federal, regional and local governments, and similar clients in each of the 50 US states, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia.  In 2026 Engineering News Record ranked HDR fifth in size of business in the important water supply and treatment category.  We have over 475 employees in this MS spanning the range of services from utility master planning, program management, strategic advisory services, transmission and distribution, water supply management, water treatment and reuse, construction management and inspection, and asset management and operations assistance.

The Drinking Water MS is comprised of a multi-layer organization to drive business and client development, while at the same time defining and implementing strategic drinking water initiatives for growth, coordinating best practices and quality professional services, and projecting the HDR brand in the marketplace.  Specific attention is required to capture the potential of the wide spectrum of employees throughout the Sector, while at the same time developing and reinforcing the image of HDR with our clients across the various drinking water markets.  

Business Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water Market Sector BDD primary performance metric is achieving NFB goals for the sector. You will provide leadership and substantial support to assessing the Regional and Area marketplace positioning and determining optimal technical strategies needed to win and secure contracts and expand business. Business development efforts will extend across all business groups to coordinate with other Architecture, Transportation, Resources, Water, BES and Federal Business Group market sectors.  This position will implement cross sector initiatives including One Water, the Value of Water, and other Sector strategies that are effective in gaining market share, and that will successfully interface with Regional/Area client development programs, our Strategic Pursuits program, and Regional/Area marketing managers/pursuit leaders. Specific business development activities include:

Incorporate our HDR and Water business vision within the market sector to become the industry leader.

Serve as the Client Manager for selected key clients within the Sector and be active and visible in the industry.

Serve as Pursuit Leader on select drinking water opportunities, leading by example in the development of pursuit strategies, proposal development and interview preparation.

Work with client managers to promote the marketing and delivery of all HDR services to Drinking Water clients across all HDR geographies.

Participate as a member of the Water Business Group Management and the National Drinking Water Market Sector Leadership Team support the coordinated development of international markets in Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, in support of broader Water Business Group international growth initiatives. Work with Regional Business Group Managers and Client Development Leadership in the development and delivery of MS initiatives that align with area and regional drivers.

Work with the client development leaders to support client development, deploy pursuit strategies, and guide pursuit processes, based on proven capture techniques.

Provide direct support to selected pursuits through client relationship development and/or through development of strategy, technical differentiation, and participation in related pursuit activities.

Actively participate in industry associations in leadership roles and serve as a company role-model in business and community organizations.

Identify key investments (acquisitions and technology) that will maintain or drive HDR into an industry leadership position.

Maintain awareness of Area marketing capabilities and provide market sector support to Areas toward achieving Drinking Water MS booking goals. 

Develop relationships with industry counterparts in other consulting and construction organizations. 

Develop relationships with senior leadership in key client organizations.

Staff Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water MS BDD will seek opportunities to enhance our performance to win new work within the marketplace and provide opportunities for staff growth and development.  Through pursuit leadership and involvement, strategically align Drinking Water staff and projects to develop and deepen skills, while mentoring and growing their capabilities and talent. Lead and/or assist with the identification and recruitment of prospective future market sector employees.

Work with the Drinking Water MS leader, Business Class Directors, and practice groups to drive technical excellence and coordinate technical staff to promote quality delivery and our Drive to Zero initiative. 

Coordinate staffing/recruiting plans for key hires and assist local leadership as necessary with local hires. Identify resource gaps and support talent management and recruiting.

Support to Key Project/Program Delivery –
 The Drinking Water MS BDD will assist Regional and Area Business Group leadership in key project delivery within the market sector.  Key responsibilities consist of helping to drive client management, acting as Principal in Charge on key project delivery, and supporting the QA/QC program to provide for successful project delivery. Facilitate cooperation and eliminate hurdles and barriers to success. Work with a business group leadership to implement process improvements and leverage work sharing to meet or exceed planned goals.

Be aware of staff workload and facilitate work sharing within the market sector; promote effective use of company resources and assist in applying key staff/expertise to projects. 

Assist with contract review on key projects to help ensure risk management, proper staffing, quality reviews and resolution of claims.

Take on Principal in Charge assignments that leverage this leadership role by driving client satisfaction, staff development, technical excellence and mentoring opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum 20 + years of experience in drinking water planning and engineering design, client development, and project management; much of that experience must reside within servicing of drinking water public and private clients and utilities.
Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in an accredited civil or environmental engineering program.
Maintain a professional engineering registration.
Experienced in development and management of strategic positioning and technical differentiation for planning and/or engineering services.
Experienced in development and management of a wide range of client relationships and specific program and/or project pursuits.
Experienced in overall staff development to include recruiting, career path development, and professional growth.
Experienced with industry associations and maintains an active and visible profile in the market sector.
Ability to work cooperatively with Market Sector Directors, Business Class Directors, Regional Business Group Director, Area Business Group Managers, Area Marketing Managers and Area Manager.
Demonstrated commitment to HDR values. An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must.

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 15 years relevant industry experience
Demonstrated "self-starter" with a history of completing projects with limited oversight
Deep knowledge of the A/E/C industry's standard approach to procurement of professional services
Demonstrated ability to motivate and inspire others
Demonstrated ability to build a network of clients and industry partners
Experience in sales and developing effective win strategies
Strong financial acumen and negotiation skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability and desire to travel and engage with others in-person
Demonstrated experience in growing programs in new or highly competitive markets
Demonstrated experience in winning high-value contracts in the A/E/C industry
Demonstrated experience in writing compelling content based on information from technical staff

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. The expected compensation range for this position is $176,000 - $315,000 depending upon skills, experience, education and geographical location. (Stated benefits are for full-time regular positions. Under the supervision of the Air Resources Supervisor I (ARS I), the APS in AMB will apply scientific methods and principles to conduct ambient air monitoring at assigned sites, in support of CARB's air pollution programs. Job Title: Environmental Scientist II

Location: Pleasanton, CA

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is currently seeking an Environmental Scientist II to support environmental restoration projects for federal government clients including USEPA, USACE, USAF, NASA, and various agencies across the United States and territories. Projects commonly involve investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by emerging contaminants (PFAS), chlorinated solvents, and petroleum compounds as well as abandoned mine lands.

The Environmental Scientist II will work out of our Pleasanton, CA office, unless on field assignments. This role requires travel of up to 50%, primarily within the Western US, but may include occasional travel across the US.

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Ensuring field operations are conducted in a safe manner in accordance with project specific Site Safety and Health Plans / Health and Safety Plans.
Participating in field teams for collection of water, soil, soil vapor, surface water and sediment samples utilizing various sampling techniques.
Performing / conducting field subcontractor oversight inclusive of drilling, monitoring well construction, waste transportation and disposal, and heavy equipment operation.
Contributing to the preparation of work plans and project deliverables (e.g., UFP-QAPPs, RI Reports, SSHP/HASPs, power point presentations, and technical memoranda).
Assisting with data entry, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical and visualization tools.
Assisting with proposals, cost estimates, and subcontractor procurement.
Potentially assisting with remedial system operations and maintenance services.
Managing / Leading field teams collecting general field data and completing environmental sampling.
Utilize approved digital and AI-assisted tools, where appropriate, to support technical documentation, data analysis, project communications, and workflow efficiency.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

2+ years of directly related experience in the environmental industry .
Strong technical writing and documentation experience with prior experience contributing to the preparation of technical reports, memoranda, and work plans.
Previous experience with environmental investigations including various groundwater, soil, and surface water/sediment methodologies.
Experience with monitoring well drilling, logging, installation and sampling; developing boring logs and review/interpretation of geological boring logs.
Ability to work within a team environment with corporate, project, and technical management staff.
Excellent interpersonal communication skills (both written and oral) including the ability to comfortably engage with varying levels of leadership, subcontractors, internal and external stakeholders.
Proficient in MS Word, MS Excel, and other MS Office applications.
Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Hydrogeology, Geophysics, Geological/Geotechnical Engineering or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Master’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Geophysics, Geological/geotechnical Engineering or a related field.
HAZWOPER 40-hour training.
Experience as a Task Manager or Field Team Leader for environmental investigations.
Knowledge and experience of CERCLA, DoD, DOE, EPA, and/or RCRA projects.
PFAS sampling or remediation experience.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIRMENTS

Ability to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time.
Prolonged standing up to 70% of the time.
Walking over uneven or mountainous terrain.
Viewing computer screen for extended periods.
Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps, graphs, warning indicators, etc.).
Driving a company or personal vehicle.
Complex problem solving and decision making.
Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations.
Communicating effectively with clients, team members, and stakeholders.
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities.

Work Environment Requirements

Must be able to work outdoors in adverse weather conditions (heat, cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must be able to travel up to 50% of the year.
May work in environments with loud noises, dust, or hazardous materials.
Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Office work environment.
Potential for longer days up to 12 hours in duration.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

HGL office work is dictated by a 5-day work week; however, fieldwork schedules will deviate based on job requirements and may require longer hours and weekends.

:

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. We believe that we can make a difference in improving the world we live in through collaboration, teamwork, and a positive work environment. With over 550 employees, HGL is large enough to execute high-profile projects, but small enough to develop personal working environments with our talented team members. By joining HGL, you will be working toward restoring the environment and protecting our future.

Job Description

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. Employees at all levels of the agency work together to foster fairness, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We strive to be a workplace where we share our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals, and while collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations. We celebrate and appreciate diversity, champion equity, and treat each other with respect and dignity.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status , gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, age, or physical or mental disability in the administration of our programs and activities. Visit DEQ’s Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page .

Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?
If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full-time opportunity available for an Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)
in Medford, Oregon.

Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

About DEQ!

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.

The Water Quality Division’s mission is to protect and improve Oregon's water quality. Protecting Oregon's rivers, lakes, streams, and groundwater quality keeps these waters safe for a multitude of beneficial uses such as drinking water, fish habitat, recreation, and irrigation. This is accomplished by developing and implementing water quality standards and clean water plans; regulating sewage treatment systems, industrial dischargers, and individual onsite septic systems; collecting and evaluating water quality data; providing grants and technical assistance to reduce non-point pollution sources; and providing loans to communities to build treatment facilities.

Over 30% of Oregonians dispose of wastewater from their homes and businesses through the use of septic systems. The siting, design, installation, and ongoing operation and maintenance of septic systems, as well as sewage disposal service licensing, are regulated through the Onsite Wastewater Management Program. Without this oversight, septic systems can fail or malfunction and sewage may be disposed of improperly, thus polluting Oregon’s land and waterways with raw sewage and creating public health hazards.

The Onsite Wastewater Management Program (septic systems) is administered through intergovernmental agreements for 33 counties and is directly administered by DEQ in 3 counties. This position will support Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will serve as an Onsite Wastewater Management Program technical expert in the evaluation, inspection, and permitting of onsite septic systems in Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties. Hundreds of onsite applications are submitted to the Medford office each year from individual homeowners, small businesses, and licensed installers. In addition to these applications, the Medford office receives technical questions from the public regarding the program’s requirements and the care and maintenance of septic systems. The office also receives complaints regarding potential septic system violations, some of which can lead to enforcement actions. In addition, local interested parties occasionally request the assistance of the local onsite technical expert to attend meetings and present information.

What’s in it for you!

The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

This is a full-time, AFSCME represented position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

What are we looking for?

Minimum Qualifications for Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist:

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration).
10 hours of soil science courses in Introductory Soil Science, Soil Morphology, Physical Geology, and Geomorphology.

Minimum Qualifications For Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities
Registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Agency as an Environmental Health Specialist Trainee or Waste Water Specialist Trainee. See the Environmental Health Registration Board’s requirements for registration. (Applicants do not need to have current registration at the time of hire, but must demonstrate that they meet the requirements to obtain a trainee registration within 30 days of employment.)

Substitutions

Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.
Master’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 4 of the required years of experience.
Doctorate degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 5 of the required years of experience.

The underfill option is available to you if you do not meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist upon hire. In order to retain this appointment, you must be able to meet the minimum qualifications for the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist by obtaining your Environmental Health Specialist or Waste Water Specialist registration by the Oregon Health Licensing Office and by completing 10 hours of soil science courses within 3 years of employment. Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration. If hired as an underfill, you will be brought in at the Natural Resource Specialist 3 salary scale instead of the Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist salary scale.

Candidates who are most competitive will also reflect the following desired attributes:

Demonstrated understanding of environmental justice and the historical impacts for marginalized and underrepresented communities; ability to take personal responsibility for increasing their knowledge of environmental justice and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Knowledge and skill in the classification, characteristics, and behavior of soils and the transport of water and wastewater through soils is required.
Knowledge of onsite wastewater treatment system technology and requirements for permitting; experience inspecting and evaluating onsite septic systems.
Experience investigating environmental complaints.
Experience reviewing design plans for new construction, alterations, and repairs of wastewater treatment systems.
Experience regulating sewage treatment systems including issuing permits and authorizations for new construction, alterations, or repairs of onsite septic systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to provide clear, concise, and compelling communication of policy and technical information tailored to the needs of diverse audiences; skill in writing and presenting clear and concise reports that include qualitative and quantitative analyses, recommendations, and conclusions to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated experience building and fostering relationships with a diverse group of partners including colleagues, interested parties, communities, organizations, and businesses.

Working Conditions

DEQ believes in a diverse and inclusive work environment. All employees are expected to contribute to a work environment that collectively values and benefits from respecting its diversity and promotes a culture of inclusiveness.

This position will be based out of DEQ’s Medford office; however, the successful candidate may be eligible for hybrid work. The logistics of hybrid work will need to be worked out with the Hiring Manager prior to your hire and may be changed at any time given specific job duties and business needs. DEQ will provide necessary hardware (laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cell phone) for an employee to successfully work from home. At DEQ sites, you will have access to a workspace, however, it may be shared with other employees.

This position requires frequent travel by car statewide for meetings, trainings, public hearings, conferences, workshops, seminars, and field visits (such as wastewater treatment facilities, land application sites, and spill or complaint sites). During field visits, there is the potential for exposure to pollutants, pathogens or hazardous materials, chemicals, contaminated soil and water, fumes, airborne contaminants, challenging field conditions (steep slopes, heavy vegetation, and uneven terrain), and inclement weather. Evening and weekend work, as well as overnight stays, will occur.

Because this work requires the incumbent to operate a motor vehicle, personal or state-owned, the incumbent must have a valid driver’s license and complete the defensive driving safety class every two (2) years.

The reporting location for this position is Sacramento, CA. This position will work under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory).


The California Ocean Protection Council (OPC) is hiring an Environmental Scientist to help advance efforts to conserve coastal, marine, and estuarine biodiversity in California. This includes conserving 30 percent of California’s coastal waters by 2030, adaptively managing California’s marine protected area network, improving coordination of coastal, marine, and estuarine monitoring and data management, and strengthening conservation at California’s land\-sea interface.


The Environmental Scientist will be responsible for collaborating with other OPC staff, state and federal regulatory agencies, California Native American tribes, academic scientists, non\-profits, community representatives, and others to advance OPC’s strategic priorities related to coastal, marine, and estuarine biodiversity. The Environmental Scientist will also be responsible for grant and contract management including developing scopes of work and budgets, tracking deliverables, and coordinating with grantees. Overall, this role will be responsible for supporting implementation of OPC’s mission and California Natural Resources Agency’s (CNRA) policy initiatives, which include embedding equity and environmental justice into programs and actions to support statewide efforts to enhance, protect, and restore biodiversity.


Applicants should have a strong scientific background, working knowledge of coastal and ocean issues and stakeholders in California, and experience working on projects and/or research related to coastal, marine, and estuarine biodiversity in California or elsewhere. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, the ability to become proficient in new and emerging topics, and the ability to work in a fast\-paced environment and prioritize tasks are a must. ### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you have a passion to perform a variety of scientific, analytical, and technical assistance duties to implement enforcement requirements and assist with program analysis of compliance policies for CalRecycle’s Responsible Textile Recovery Act of 2024? Do you enjoy working in a collaborative, dynamic environment? CalRecycle is seeking an enthusiastic Environmental Scientist to join our talented team that is passionate to work in Textiles Unit!  

  

**Position Description**
Under the direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist (incumbent) at Range A (an entry level employee) works under direct supervision performing the least complex scientific work; at Range B (an intermediate level employee) works under general supervision performing moderately complex work; or at Range C (a journey person level employee) works independently performing the most complex work. The Environmental Scientist (ES) will have a variety of responsibilities from scientific, analytical, and administrative duties to implement and enforce the Responsible Textile Recovery Act of 2024 within the Textiles Unit. The incumbent applies the principles of scientific research and analytical skills to perform complex technical tasks and uses statistical knowledge to gather, assess, and review data in order to ensure their compliance with CalRecycle's producer responsibility and product stewardship requirements and regulations. The incumbent is responsible for the determination of violations and their general effects on public health, safety, and the environment for the programs, reviewing findings and preparing the reports for technical adequacy on enforcement matters, and doing other related work to perform the duties listed below. Additionally, the ES will play an important role in developing and implementing new enforcement programs related to products with EPR and product stewardship requirements.  

  

The Program is responsible for compliance and enforcement related to producer responsibility, product stewardship and seeks to enforce EPR laws governing the regulated communities including, but not limited to: Producer Responsibility Organizations (PRO), producers/manufacturers of covered products, licensees of trademarks or brands, importers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers and other regulated parties. The incumbent will determine if regulated communities are in compliance by performing field inspections and investigations. On a daily basis, conduct research of businesses, products, and industries to plan inspections and conduct investigations; develop sound conclusions and recommendations for the issuance of timely, concise and complete inspection reports; and compile defensible facts for legal documents. Serve as an EPR compliance program liaison and educate stakeholders verbally and in writing; accurately explain the law and potential enforcement consequences; prepare correspondence; meet regulatory deadlines; and implement established enforcement processes. Work in coordination with CalRecycle’s other supporting technical staff and the Legal Office; evaluate the significance of violations of non\-compliant entities and program trends; compile, organize data and use mathematical formulas and develop databases and tools to perform statistical analyses to track compliance trends of the regulated community to evaluate overall program success; recommend corrective actions or penalties and fines to effectively achieve the program(s) mandates to protect public health and safety and the environment. Prepare findings to present and conduct technical trainings to supervisors, technical offices, Executive Management and Stakeholders.
  

  

This position involves traveling throughout California involving multiple, consecutive days away from the office and overnight stays. The incumbent must have a current California Driver’s License and participate in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Employer Pull Notice Program.
  

  

**As of July 1st, 2026, the position is office\-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.  

  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The 40\-hour work week schedule is typically dayshift, Monday through Friday. Office and field work includes, on a regular basis, writing and reviewing inspection reports and notices, contact with the regulated community by way of in\-person, phone and video conferencing, preparation and review of other documents and internet research. Overnight travel may be required locally and within the state. The job occasionally requires you to perform field inspections, hear vehicles and alarms or other audible signals of possible risk.

T\&B Planning’s Environmental Analysts work in a collaborative environment preparing CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for land development, policy planning, and infrastructure projects. Environmental Analysts are primarily responsible for research and analysis, keeping project files organized, reviewing and proofreading technical reports, and writing environmental compliance documents. Document types include Environmental Impact Reports or Statements (EIR/EIS), Mitigated Negative Declarations (MNDs), Addenda, Findings, Environmental Assessments (EAs) and public notices. Environmental Analysts also assist Project Managers with preparing meeting agendas, collecting and distributing meeting notes, tracking project status, and schedule management. Opportunities are provided for on\-the\-job training and professional development.


The position of Environmental Analyst is ideal for an early career candidate with fewer than 7 years of CEQA or NEPA document preparation experience, who enjoys both autonomous and collaborative work environments, and can commit to working full time. In\-office and hybrid positions are available, with preference given to candidates who can commit to working at least one day per week in person in Irvine CA, San Diego CA, Pittsburgh PA or Portland OR.


Requirements:
* Prepare CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents
* Writing, proofreading and editing
* Data collection and analysis
* Schedule tracking and management
* Organization of project files
* Research planning, zoning, entitlement permits, and environmental clearances
* Attend meetings and public hearings remotely and/or in person
* Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree; preferably in environmental studies, urban planning, writing, public administration, or project management
* Strong organizational, writing, and proofreading skills
* Proficient in MS Word, Outlook, and Excel
* Effective and collaborative communicator
* Motivated toward career advancement

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real\-world impact.


“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.


When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.


Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.


**A Day in the Life**
---------------------
